text:
183. The UN Refugee Convention defines a “refugee” as someone who, “owing to a well-founded
fear of being persecuted for reasons of race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular
social group, or political opinion, is outside the country of his nationality, and is unable to or,
owing to such fear, is unwilling to, avail himself of the protection of that country”. A refugee is
a person who has been granted asylum.

184. Gypsy: Some people from the GRT communities find the term “gypsy” offensive, whereas
others are proud to use that term. Judges should ask the person how they identify.

185. British/English: “British” and “English” are used to refer to nationalities first and foremost,
which include people of all ethnic groups.

186. Welsh: If in Wales, a reference to “Welsh people” should not mean only those who speak
Welsh. A Welsh person, who speaks only English, is still Welsh. It would be wrong, for
example, to describe a witness who gives evidence in Welsh as “the Welsh witness”, which
may be taken to mean that others are therefore not Welsh. Unlike the English language, the
Welsh language has slightly different words for “Welsh” in the sense of the language
(“Cymraeg”) and “Welsh” in the sense of “of Wales” (“Cymreig”). This could lead to
misunderstandings in translation.
